title: Comparing Income and Age in Florida
text:
Click on any county in the map above to see its exact median household income and median age. This map divides Florida’s 67 counties into four categories by comparing each county’s median household income and median age against the statewide county medians:

High Income, Older: Concentrated along the Gulf and Atlantic coastlines (such as Collier, Sarasota, St. Johns, and Martin counties), reflecting affluent coastal and retirement communities.
High Income, Younger: Clustered around major metropolitan job hubs like Orange (Orlando), Hillsborough (Tampa), Duval (Jacksonville), and Miami-Dade counties.
Low Income, Older: Found mostly in rural inland and central Florida retirement counties (such as Citrus, Highlands, and Marion counties) where the cost of living is lower.
Low Income, Younger: Concentrated in inland agricultural counties and counties with large university populations, such as Alachua (Gainesville) and Leon (Tallahassee).
